KNOWN GAP, PINNED. The link rule matches a bare domain only against a FINITE TLD list, so .zip/.tk/.top/.buzz/.online all pass. A whitelist can never be complete. Broadening to any word.word would start refusing node.js and U.S.A, which is a worse trade for a box people write prose into. What actually stops this reaching the site is pre-moderation: nothing publishes without an explicit approval, so an uncaught link costs one line in a queue the owner reads.
Cyrillic letters survive NFKC but still match a word character run before an ASCII TLD, so the bare-domain branch catches it. Kept as a win, not a gap.
